Tuesday, December 3, 1963 FEDERAL REGISTER 12787
v  Executive Order 11129
DESIGNATING CERTAIN FACILITIES OF THE NATIONAL AERONAUTICS
AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION AND OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DE­
FENSE, IN THE STATE OF FLORIDA, AS THE JOHN F. KENNEDY
SPACE CENTER
W HEREAS President John F. Kennedy lighted the imagination  
of our people when he set the moon as our -target and man as the  
means to reach it ;  and
W HEREAS the installations now to be renamed are a center and  
symbol of our country’s peaceful assault on space; and
W HEREAS it is in the nature of this assault that it should test  
the limits of our youth and grace, our strength and wit, our vigor  
and perseverance—qualities fitting to the memory of John F. Kennedy:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me as  
President of the United States, I hereby designate the facilities of  
the Launch Operations Center of the National Aeronautics and Space  
Administration and the facilities of Station No. 1 of the Atlantic  
Missile Range, in the State of Florida, as the John F. Kennedy Space  
Center; and such facilities shall be hereafter known and referred to  
by that name.
L yndon  B. J ohnson
T h e W hite  H ouse,
November 29,1963.
[F.R. Doc. 63-12542; Filed, Nov. 29,1963 :  4 :13 p.m.]

research_rationale:
EO 11129 (Johnson, signed 1963-11-29, 28 FR 12787, Federal Register of 1963-12-03) designates the facilities of the Launch Operations Center of NASA and of Station No. 1 of the Atlantic Missile Range in Florida as the John F. Kennedy Space Center and directs that they be known by that name. The held text is a single sentence with no expiry or condition. The Federal Register disposition notes name no amendment or revocation. The current U.S. Code, 51 U.S.C. 20306(a)(6)(B) (added by Pub. L. 119-21, title IV, section 40005(a), July 4, 2025), refers to the center described in Executive Order 11129 (28 Fed. Reg. 12787), which shows the designation is treated as in effect. The order cites no statute as authority (it relies on the President's constitutional authority), so no authority statute needs checking.

EO 10860 (Eisenhower, signed 1960-02-05, 25 FR 1089, published 1960-02-09) prescribes the design of the Coat of Arms of the President (section 1), the Seal of the President (section 2), the Color and Flag of the President (section 3), makes the designs, as shown in the accompanying illustrations and specifications, exclusive to the President (section 4), and provides that it becomes effective on July 4, 1960 when it supersedes EO 10823 of May 26, 1959 (section 5). The dossier inventory ran sections 2 and 3 together because the OCR prints the section 3 marker with a doubled period, so the inventory is corrected with overrides to five scopes covering every section of the held text. The text has no expiry or condition, and a search of the held corpus for the order number finds only its own text and the 1989 codification. The Federal Register disposition note records only that it supersedes EO 10823. The U.S. Code and eCFR bounded searches found no hit, and the machine searches record no amendment or revocation, so the claim rests on the held original plus those bounded searches; this is a negative-search predicate, and the accompanying illustrations and specifications are not held.

Each is treated separately; none depends on the order ending in part."}
